text:
### Observed differences

- Participation around a former either-or choice changed sharply. In the earlier window, A22 ran in 54 of 100 traces and each of A31, A32 and A37 in about 46 of 100 (92 of 200 traces), always exactly once when present; in the later window, A22 ran in all 200 traces and A31, A32 and A37 in about 199 of 200, once per trace [OCC019, OCC020, OCC021, OCC026].
- The either-or choice itself disappeared. Before, about 54 of 100 of A21's observed outgoing transitions went to A22 and about 46 of 100 went into the group A31/A32/A37, and A22 never shared a trace with any group member; in the later window, A21 led to A22 in essentially every case, and A22 co-occurred with each group member in about 995 of 1000 traces, with the group running first [DIR015, REL011, REL012, REL013].
- The group changed place. Before, A20 was followed directly by A23 in all of its observed outgoing transitions; after, A23's share fell to nearly zero while A31, A32 and A37 took about a third each [DIR014]. The group's exits moved from A26 (about 29–36 in 100 of its outgoing transitions before) to A23 (about 31–37 in 100 after) [DIR018, DIR019, DIR024]. The distance from A20 to A23 grew from one step in every trace to four steps in about 995 of 1000, so the three group activities now sit between them [LAG001].
- The tail of the segment became uniform. The A21-to-A26 distance was two steps in 54 of 100 traces and four steps in 46 of 100 before; after, it is two steps in every trace, consistent with A21, then A22, then A26, with A22 preceding A26 and A23 preceding A22 in all traces (54 of 100 before) [LAG002, REL010, REL005, REL009].
- Relative event positions agree with this re-wiring: the group's mean position moved from about 0.59 to about 0.40 of the trace, A23's from about 0.39 to 0.46, A22's from 0.59 (in 54 of 100 traces) to 0.63 (all traces), and A21's from 0.54 to 0.60 [POS006, POS007, POS008, POS004, POS003, POS002].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

A structural re-wiring of the segment around A20, A21, A22, A23, A26 and the group A31/A32/A37 is supported by the evidence. In the earlier window, every case ran A20 then A23 and later A21, which was followed either by A22 and then A26 (about 54 in 100 cases) or by the group A31/A32/A37 and then A26 (about 46 in 100), the two being mutually exclusive; in the later window, that choice no longer exists — the group runs in every case between A20 and A23, and A21 always leads to A22, which precedes A26 in every case. A22 and the group each became mandatory, their exclusive routing was removed, and the group's position moved from after A21 to between A20 and A23 [OCC019, OCC020, OCC021, OCC026, DIR014, DIR015, DIR018, DIR019, DIR024, REL011, LAG001, LAG002].

The change is shown directly, not inferred from frequencies alone: successor profiles changed at A20 and at all three group activities, relation items flipped from zero co-occurrence to near-universal co-occurrence with a fixed order, and the lag items change exactly as this re-wiring predicts. About 40 items across occurrence, direction, relation, lag and position indicators describe this single difference, each with empirical strength of about 0.995, and every involved activity appeared in a substantial share of traces (about 46–54 in 100) in both windows, so a rare-variant explanation does not fit [DIR014, DIR018, REL011, REL014, LAG001, LAG002, POS006].

Limitations: direction profiles cover only observed outgoing transitions, so the evidence cannot distinguish newly added edges from pre-existing but previously unobserved or very rare edges that now dominate; the order of A23 relative to A21 in the later window rests on event positions rather than a direct relation item; and the evidence includes no chance-expectation baseline, so the judgement rests on the directness and consistency of the relational items [DIR014, POS004, POS002].

Other differences: a few small redistributions of a few percentage points, consistent with sampling variation between two 200-trace windows — A40's split between A14 and A15 moved from about 46/54 to about 53/47, A18's outgoing share to A27 rose from about 39 to 58 in 100, A44 led to A45 somewhat more often (about 53 to 61 in 100), and A10 and A11 repeated slightly more often per trace [DIR026, OCC013, OCC014, DIR012, DIR029, OCC009, OCC010].
